projectInstructions:
Answer all questions in the style of a friendly colleague, using informal language.

Follow standard Rust formatting and linting rules.

Before making code changes:
- Ask if there is an existing GitHub issue for the change
- If no issue exists, create one using gh CLI
- Include current behavior, expected behavior, implementation approach
- Use issue discussions to track implementation decisions
- Reference issue numbers in commit messages

Use conventional commits format for all commit messages:
- feat: new features
- fix: bug fixes
- docs: documentation changes
- style: formatting changes
- refactor: code restructuring
- test: adding tests
- chore: maintenance tasks
- ci: CI/CD changes
- perf: performance improvements
- build: build system changes

When referencing issues in commits:
- For fixes, use "fixes #X" or "resolves #X"
- For related changes, use "relates to #X"
- Place issue references on a new line in commit message body
editInstructions:
When suggesting code changes:
- Follow Rust best practices
- Ensure code is properly formatted
- Include necessary error handling
- Add appropriate comments for complex logic
toolInstructions:
When working with the codebase:
- Prefer semantic search for context gathering
- Make sure to validate changes with proper error checking
- Use appropriate GRust tools and commands
- Validate issue references in commits
